title: Madaniyatlararo farqlar
goal_uz: Dars oxirida ingliz tilida Britaniya va AQSh madaniy normalarini tushuntirasiz, muloyim va ochiq gapirish farqini ishlatasiz, madaniy xatolardan qochasiz va madaniyatlarni hurmat bilan solishtirasiz.

scenes.title: Madaniyatlararo farqlar
scenes.say_native: Assalomu alaykum! Oldingi darsda media, reklama va yangiliklar tilini o‘rgandik. Bugun tilning orqasidagi narsa haqida gaplashamiz: madaniyat. Grammatikani yaxshi bilib ham, noto‘g‘ri tushunilib qolish mumkin. Dars oxirida mamlakatlarning odatlarini, muloyimlik va ochiqlik farqini tushuntirasiz va madaniyatlarni hurmat bilan solishtirasiz.
scenes.say: Hello again! Last time we looked at the media. Today we look at what sits behind the language: culture. By the end, you will explain differences, avoid awkward mistakes and compare cultures with respect.
scenes.say_uz: Yana salom! Bugun tilning orqasidagi narsani, ya'ni madaniyatni ko‘ramiz. Farqlarni tushuntirib, xatolardan qochib, hurmat bilan solishtirasiz.

scenes.title: Umumlashtirish haqida ogohlantirish

examples.t: Many British people tend to queue politely.
examples.uz: Ko‘p britaniyaliklar odatda navbatda odob bilan turishadi.

scenes.say_native: Har bir madaniyatda yozilmagan qoidalar bor: qachon kelish, nimani so‘ramaslik, qanday rad etish. Lekin bugun aytadigan hamma narsa moyillik, qat'iy qoida emas. Har bir inglizning o‘z odati bor. Shuning uchun “many”, “often” va “tend to” kabi so‘zlarni ishlatamiz. Hurmat bilan gapirish aynan shunday boshlanadi.
scenes.say: Every culture has unwritten rules. But everything today describes tendencies, not fixed rules. That is why we say many, often and tend to.
scenes.say_uz: Har bir madaniyatda yozilmagan qoidalar bor, lekin bugun aytilganlar moyillik, qoida emas. Shuning uchun many, often, tend to deymiz.

scenes.title: Small talk va “How are you?”

examples.t: A: How are you? B: Fine, thanks. You?
Lovely weather today, isn't it?

scenes.say_native: Birinchi nuqta: Buyuk Britaniya va AQSh odatlari. Notanish odam bilan ob-havo yoki dam olish kunlari haqida mayda gaplashish, ya'ni small talk normal. “How are you?” esa ko‘pincha savol emas, salom. Unga qisqa javob beriladi: “Fine, thanks, you?” Kasalliklaringizni tushuntirib o‘tirmang, o‘zbekchadagi batafsil hol-ahvol so‘rashdan ancha qisqa.
scenes.say: Small talk matters in Britain and the USA. And how are you is usually a greeting, not a real question. Keep your answer short: fine, thanks, you?
scenes.say_uz: Small talk muhim. How are you odatda salom, javob qisqa bo‘ladi: fine, thanks, you?

scenes.title: Navbat madaniyati
board: Jump the queue = cut in line (navbatni buzish)

examples.t: Sorry, were you here before me?

scenes.say_native: Navbat Britaniyada queue, Amerikada line deyiladi. Britaniyada navbatni buzish, ya'ni “jump the queue”, odamlarni qattiq ranjitadi, hatto ular hech narsa demasa ham. Shubha bo‘lsa, muloyim so‘rang: “Sorry, were you here before me?” Bu ibora sizni qutqaradi.
scenes.say: The British say queue, Americans say line. Jumping the queue upsets people, even if they stay silent. If unsure, ask: sorry, were you here before me?
scenes.say_uz: Britaniyada queue, AQShda line. Navbatni buzish odamlarni ranjitadi. Shubha bo‘lsa: sorry, were you here before me?

scenes.title: Vaqt, masofa va ismlar
board: Personal space: about an arm's length
'Please, call me Tom.' — use first names

examples.t: I'm sorry, I'm running late.

scenes.say_native: Ishda, uchrashuvda va shifokorda aniq vaqtda kelish kutiladi. Kechiksangiz, oldindan xabar bering: “I'm sorry, I'm running late.” Odamlar odatda qo‘l uzunligicha masofada turishadi. Ishda ham ko‘pincha ism bilan murojaat qilinadi. Janob Braun “Please, call me Tom” desa, ismini ayting. Ular odamga qarab o‘zgaradi, shuning uchun atrofga qarab moslashing.
scenes.say: Be on time for work and appointments, and message if you will be late. People often stand about an arm's length apart, and first names are common at work.
scenes.say_uz: Ishda o‘z vaqtida keling, kechiksangiz xabar bering. Masofa qo‘l uzunligicha, ishda ism bilan murojaat qilinadi.

scenes.title: Tip va hisob
board: Pub: pay at the bar; 'a round'

examples.t: Is service included?
It's my round.

scenes.say_native: Britaniyadagi restoranlarda hisobga ko‘pincha taxminan o‘n–o‘n ikki yarim foiz xizmat haqi qo‘shiladi, shuning uchun so‘rang: “Is service included?” Amerikada esa tip, ya'ni choy puli, deyarli majburiy, odatda o‘n besh–yigirma foiz. Britaniya pablarida buyurtmani bar oldida berib, o‘sha yerda to‘laysiz. Do‘stlar navbatma-navbat ichimlik oladi, bu “a round” deyiladi.
scenes.say: In British restaurants, service is often added to the bill, so ask: is service included? In the USA, tipping is expected, usually fifteen to twenty percent. In a pub, you pay at the bar.
scenes.say_uz: Britaniyada xizmat haqi ko‘pincha qo‘shiladi, so‘rang. AQShda tip kutiladi, 15–20 foiz. Pabda bar oldida to‘laysiz.

scenes.title: Haqiqiy taklif emas
board: ✓ Real invitation: a day and a time

examples.t: Are you free on Thursday at one?

scenes.say_native: Keng tarqalgan xato: kimdir “Let's have lunch sometime” desa, ko‘pincha bu shunchaki odob, haqiqiy taklif emas. O‘zbek madaniyatida taklif aniq va samimiy bo‘ladi, shuning uchun siz kutib qolishingiz mumkin. Haqiqiy taklifda kun va vaqt bo‘ladi. Siz ham ko‘rishmoqchi bo‘lsangiz, aniq kunni o‘zingiz taklif qiling.
scenes.say: When someone says, let's have lunch sometime, it is often just politeness. A real invitation has a day and a time. If you want to meet, suggest it yourself.
scenes.say_uz: Let's have lunch sometime ko‘pincha shunchaki odob. Haqiqiy taklifda kun va vaqt bo‘ladi. Ko‘rishmoqchi bo‘lsangiz, o‘zingiz taklif qiling.

scenes.title: To‘g‘ri yoki noto‘g‘ri?
board: 1) 'Fine, thanks' is a normal answer to 'How are you?'
2) In Britain, jumping the queue is fine if you are quick.
3) 'Let's have lunch sometime' always has a date.
4) In a US restaurant, no tip is normal.
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta gapni eshiting, har biri to‘g‘rimi yoki noto‘g‘rimi, ayting. Birinchi: “How are you?” ga “Fine, thanks” normal. Ikkinchi: tez bo‘lsangiz, navbatni buzsa bo‘ladi. Uchinchi: “Let's have lunch sometime” da doim sana bor. To‘rtinchi: AQShda tip bermaslik normal.
scenes.say: True or false? One: fine, thanks is normal. Two: jumping the queue is fine if you are quick. Three: let's have lunch sometime always has a date. Four: no tip is normal in the USA.
scenes.say_uz: To‘g‘ri yoki noto‘g‘ri? Bir: fine, thanks normal. Ikki: tez bo‘lsangiz navbatni buzsa bo‘ladi. Uch: har doim sana bor. To‘rt: AQShda tip bermaslik normal.

scenes.title: Javoblar
scenes.say_native: Birinchi, to‘g‘ri: qisqa javob odatiy. Ikkinchi, noto‘g‘ri: tez bo‘lish navbatni buzishni oqlamaydi. Uchinchi, noto‘g‘ri: bu ibora ko‘pincha shunchaki odob. To‘rtinchi, noto‘g‘ri: AQShda tip bermaslik odatda noto‘g‘ri qabul qilinadi. Endi ikkinchi nuqtaga o‘tamiz: muloyimlik va to‘g‘ridan-to‘g‘rilik.
scenes.say: One: true. Two: false. Three: false. Four: false. Now let's move on to politeness and directness.
scenes.say_uz: Bir to‘g‘ri, ikki noto‘g‘ri, uch noto‘g‘ri, to‘rt noto‘g‘ri. Endi muloyimlik va to‘g‘ridan-to‘g‘rilikka o‘tamiz.

scenes.title: Bilvosita gapirish
board: UK often indirect; USA often explicit

examples.t: That's quite a brave idea.
examples.uz: Bu ancha jasur g‘oya (= menda shubha bor bo‘lishi mumkin).

scenes.say_native: Ba'zi madaniyatlar fikrni ochiq aytadi, boshqalari yumshatadi va ishora qiladi. Britaniyaliklar ko‘pincha ikkinchi usulni tanlaydi: tanqidni yumshatishadi. Masalan, “That's quite a brave idea” ba'zan “menimcha, bu xavfli” degan ma'noni bildiradi. Amerikaliklar ko‘pincha ochiqroq va ijobiyroq gapiradi. Bu hamma uchun emas, lekin shu ehtimolni yodda tuting.
scenes.say: Some cultures speak directly, others soften and hint. British speakers often soften criticism. Americans are often more explicit. Not always, but keep it in mind.
scenes.say_uz: Ba'zi madaniyatlar ochiq, ba'zilari ishora bilan gapiradi. Britaniyaliklar ko‘pincha tanqidni yumshatadi, amerikaliklar ochiqroq.

scenes.title: Yumshatilgan iboralar
board: 'I'll bear it in mind' = maybe not

examples.t: I'm afraid that won't be possible.

scenes.say_native: Eshitganda qanday tushunish kerak. “I'm afraid we can't” bu qo‘rquv emas, muloyim “yo‘q”. “That's interesting” ba'zan haqiqiy qiziqish, ba'zan ehtiyotkor shubha. “I'll bear it in mind” esa ko‘pincha qat'iy va'da emas. “With respect” dan keyin odatda norozilik keladi. Shubha bo‘lsa, so‘rang: “Do you mean you'd prefer a different approach?”
scenes.say: I'm afraid we can't is a polite no. That's interesting may be doubt. I'll bear it in mind often means probably not. If unsure, check: do you mean you would prefer a different approach?
scenes.say_uz: I'm afraid we can't — muloyim yo‘q. That's interesting — shubha bo‘lishi mumkin. I'll bear it in mind — ko‘pincha yo‘q. Shubha bo‘lsa aniqlashtiring.

scenes.title: Tinglang: noaniq fikr
board: Anna: I read your report, Ali.
Anna: It's quite good, but perhaps a bit shorter?
Anna: I'd consider cutting the second section.
scenes.say_native: Dialogni tinglang. Anna Aliga hisobot haqida fikr bildiradi. U “yomon” demaydi, lekin “perhaps” va “a bit” so‘zlari bilan aslida muhim talabni aytyapti. Savollarga keyingi mashqda javob beramiz. Ularning ohangiga va yumshatuvchi so‘zlarga e'tibor bering.
scenes.say: Hi Ali, I read your report. It's quite good, but perhaps it could be a bit shorter? Which parts? Well, I'd consider cutting the second section, if you have time. No rush, of course.
scenes.say_uz: Salom Ali, hisobotingni o‘qidim. Yaxshi, lekin biroz qisqaroq bo‘lishi mumkin. Qaysi qismlar? Ikkinchi bo‘limni qisqartirishni o‘ylab ko‘rardim. Shoshilma.

scenes.title: Anna nimani kutyapti?
scenes.say_native: Uchta savol. Birinchi: Anna hisobotni yoqtiradimi? Ikkinchi: “perhaps it could be shorter” aslida nimani bildiradi? Uchinchi: Ali qaysi qismni o‘zgartirishi kerak? Baland ovozda javob bering. Ingliz tilidagi yumshoq iboralarni to‘g‘ri o‘qish aynan shu yerda mashq qilinadi.
scenes.say: One: does Anna like the report? Two: what does perhaps it could be shorter really mean? Three: which part should Ali change?
scenes.say_uz: Bir: Anna hisobotni yoqtiradimi? Ikki: perhaps shorter aslida nimani bildiradi? Uch: Ali qaysi qismni o‘zgartirishi kerak?

scenes.title: Javoblar
scenes.say_native: Birinchi: Anna hisobotni qisman yoqtiradi, “quite good”, lekin o‘zgarish istaydi. Ikkinchi: “perhaps it could be shorter” amalda “iltimos, qisqartiring” degani. Uchinchi: ikkinchi bo‘lim. Yumshoq taklifni muloyim iltimos deb o‘qing. Bu o‘zbekchadagi “Balki bir qarab chiqarsiz” iborasiga yaqin.
scenes.say: One: she partly likes it but wants changes. Two: it means, please shorten it. Three: the second section.
scenes.say_uz: Qisman yoqtiradi, o‘zgarish istaydi; qisqartiring degani; ikkinchi bo‘lim.

scenes.title: Iltimosning narvoni
board: Could I have some water, please?
Would you mind if I opened the window?
I wonder if I could ask you something.
scenes.say_native: Iltimoslar narvon kabi. Eng pastda buyruq: “Give me water”, u ingliz tilida qo‘pol eshitiladi. Yuqoriroqda “Can I have…?”, undan keyin “Could I have… please?”, yanada muloyim “Would you mind if I…?” va “I wonder if I could…”. Vaziyat qanchalik rasmiy yoki noqulay bo‘lsa, shuncha yuqoriga chiqing. Kafeda “Could I have” yetarli.
scenes.say: Requests work like a ladder. Give me water sounds rude. Higher up: can I have, could I have please, would you mind if I, and I wonder if I could. The more formal the situation, the higher you climb.
scenes.say_uz: Iltimoslar narvon kabi: give me water qo‘pol; can I, could I please, would you mind if I, I wonder if I could — tobora muloyimroq.

scenes.title: Would you mind va I wonder if
board: Would you mind if I + past simple?
I wonder if you could + base verb

examples.t: Would you mind closing the door?
Would you mind if I sat here?
I wonder if you could help me.
examples.uz: Menga yordam bera olasiz degan umiddaman.

scenes.say_native: Uchta qolip. “Would you mind” dan keyin fe'l -ing shaklida keladi: “Would you mind closing the door?” “Would you mind if I” dan keyin past simple keladi: “Would you mind if I sat here?” Bu o‘tgan zamon emas, muloyimlik uchun. “I wonder if you could” dan keyin oddiy fe'l. Rozilik uchun “Not at all” deng. Bu yerda “Yes” qarshilikni bildirishi mumkin.
scenes.say: Would you mind plus the ing form. Would you mind if I plus past simple. I wonder if you could plus base verb. To agree, say: not at all.
scenes.say_uz: Would you mind + -ing; would you mind if I + past simple; I wonder if you could + base verb. Rozi bo‘lsangiz, not at all deng.

scenes.title: O‘zbekchadan kelgan qo‘polliklar
board: ✓ Could I borrow a pen, please?
scenes.say_native: Ikki tipik xato. Birinchisi, buyruq shakli: “Give me a pen”. O‘zbekchada “Qalam bering” oddiy, lekin inglizchada buyruqdek eshitiladi. “Could I borrow a pen, please?” deng. Ikkinchisi, “You are wrong”. Uni “I'm not sure I agree” yoki “I see it a little differently” bilan almashtiring. Muloyimlik sizni zaif qilmaydi, suhbatni davom ettiradi.
scenes.say: Two typical mistakes. Give me a pen sounds like an order: say, could I borrow a pen, please? And instead of, you are wrong, say: I'm not sure I agree.
scenes.say_uz: Give me a pen buyruqdek eshitiladi, could I borrow a pen please deng. You are wrong o‘rniga I'm not sure I agree deng.

scenes.title: Muloyim qiling
scenes.say_native: Uchta qo‘pol gapni muloyim qiling. Birinchi: “Open the window.” Ikkinchi: “Tell me the time.” Uchinchi: “Send me the file.” Har biri uchun “Could you”, “Would you mind” yoki “I wonder if” dan foydalaning. Ohang haqida keyinroq gaplashamiz, hozir faqat shaklga e'tibor bering.
scenes.say: Make these three sentences polite. One: open the window. Two: tell me the time. Three: send me the file.
scenes.say_uz: Uch gapni muloyim qiling: derazani oching; vaqtni ayting; faylni yuboring.

scenes.title: Muloyim variantlar
board: 1) Would you mind opening the window?
2) Could you tell me the time, please?
3) I wonder if you could send me the file.
scenes.say_native: Namunaviy javoblar. Birinchi: “Would you mind opening the window?” Ikkinchi: “Could you tell me the time, please?” Uchinchi: “I wonder if you could send me the file.” Sizning variantingiz ham to‘g‘ri bo‘lishi mumkin, agar shakl to‘g‘ri va ohang muloyim bo‘lsa.
scenes.say: Would you mind opening the window? Could you tell me the time, please? I wonder if you could send me the file.
scenes.say_uz: Derazani ochib bera olasizmi? Vaqtni ayta olasizmi? Faylni yuborib bera olasizmi?

scenes.title: Taklifni qabul va rad etish
board: First 'no' may be taken as final!

examples.t: Would you like another slice? — Yes, please, it's delicious.
examples.uz: Yana bir bo‘lak xohlaysizmi? — Ha, iltimos, juda mazali.

scenes.say_native: Bu o‘zbek o‘quvchilari uchun muhim. O‘zbek mehmondorchiligida mezbon bir necha marta qistaydi, mehmon esa odob yuzasidan avval rad etadi. Ingliz tilli muhitda ko‘p holda birinchi javob haqiqiy javob deb olinadi. “No, thank you” desangiz, mezbon takrorlamasligi mumkin va siz och qolasiz. Xohlasangiz, birinchi marta “Yes, please” deng.
scenes.say: In Uzbek hospitality, a guest may refuse first and the host insists. In English-speaking settings, the first answer is often taken as final. If you want something, say yes please the first time.
scenes.say_uz: O‘zbek mehmondorchiligida avval rad etib, keyin qabul qilinadi. Inglizcha muhitda birinchi javob oxirgi deb olinadi, xohlasangiz yes please deng.

scenes.title: Muloyim e'tiroz
board: I see what you mean, but…

examples.t: I see what you mean, but I'd say it depends.
examples.uz: Nima demoqchiligingizni tushundim, lekin menimcha bog‘liq.

scenes.say_native: Fikr bildirganda ham shu mantiq ishlaydi. Avval suhbatdoshning gapini tan oling, keyin o‘z fikringizni ayting: “I see what you mean, but…” yoki “That's a fair point. However…”. Qat'iy bo‘lishingiz kerak bo‘lsa, “I'm afraid I disagree” ham muloyim. Faqat “No, that's not true” deb boshlamang, chunki suhbatdosh darhol himoyalanadi.
scenes.say: First acknowledge the other person, then give your view: I see what you mean, but, or that's a fair point, however. If you must be firm, I'm afraid I disagree is still polite.
scenes.say_uz: Avval suhbatdoshni tan oling, keyin fikringizni ayting: I see what you mean, but; that's a fair point, however.

scenes.title: Ohang ham muloyimlik

examples.t: Could you help me?

scenes.say_native: Muloyimlik faqat so‘zlarda emas, ohangda ham. Ha/yo‘q savollarda ovoz odatda oxirida ko‘tariladi va do‘stona eshitiladi. Bir xil past ohang sovuq tuyulishi mumkin. Tez nutqda “could you” va “would you” da “d” va “y” qo‘shilib ketadi: /kʊdʒə/ va /wʊdʒə/. Bu normal. Keling, takrorlaymiz, tabassum bilan.
scenes.say: Politeness is also tone. In yes-no questions the voice usually rises, which sounds friendly. In fast speech, could you and would you blend: could-ya, would-ya. Repeat after me, with a smile.
scenes.say_uz: Muloyimlik ohangda ham. Ha/yo‘q savollarda ovoz ko‘tariladi. Tez nutqda could you va would you qo‘shilib ketadi. Tabassum bilan takrorlang.

scenes.title: Ohang bilan takrorlang
scenes.say_native: Takrorlang. Ovozingizni oxirida ko‘taring va tabassum qiling. Har gapni ikki marta ayting. Masalan, savol oxirida ovozni biroz ko‘taring va gapni bir nafasda ayting, so‘ngra yana takrorlang. Hozir ikkala savol uchun ham xuddi shu ohangni saqlang va shoshilmang.
scenes.say: Could you help me? Would you mind waiting? Could you help me? Would you mind waiting?
scenes.say_uz: Menga yordam bera olasizmi? Kutib tura olasizmi?

scenes.title: Ohang bo‘yicha tekshiruv
scenes.say_native: Tekshiruv. Ikkala savolda ham ovoz oxirida ko‘tarilishi kerak edi. Tabassum haqiqatan ovozni yumshatadi, telefonda gaplashganda ham eshitiladi. Endi uchinchi nuqtaga o‘tamiz: madaniy xatolardan qochish. Agar ovozingiz tekis chiqqan bo‘lsa, yana bir bor urinib ko‘ring.
scenes.say: Check. In both questions, the voice should rise at the end. A smile really does warm the voice. Now let's turn to avoiding cultural mistakes.
scenes.say_uz: Ikkala savolda ovoz oxirida ko‘tariladi. Tabassum ovozni isitadi. Endi madaniy xatolardan qochishga o‘tamiz.

scenes.title: Mavzular va savollar
board: Careful: salary, age, weight, religion, politics
'How much do you earn?' — too personal

examples.t: I hope you don't mind my asking, but…

scenes.say_native: Ba'zi savollar o‘zbek madaniyatida oddiy, lekin ingliz tilli muhitda shaxsiy hisoblanadi: maosh, yosh, vazn, nikoh va bolalar haqida notanishdan so‘rash. Siyosat va din ham yangi tanishuvda noqulay bo‘lishi mumkin. So‘rash zarur bo‘lsa, yumshating: “I hope you don't mind my asking, but…”.
scenes.say: Questions about salary, age, weight, marriage and children can feel private. Politics and religion can also be risky. If you must ask, soften it: I hope you don't mind my asking, but.
scenes.say_uz: Maosh, yosh, vazn, nikoh haqidagi savollar shaxsiy. Zarur bo‘lsa yumshating: I hope you don't mind my asking, but.

scenes.title: Mehmonga borish
board: Bring a small gift: flowers, chocolates
Ask: 'Shall I take my shoes off?'
Thank the host when you leave

examples.t: Thank you for having us. The meal was delicious.
examples.uz: Bizni kutib olgani uchun rahmat. Taom juda mazali edi.

scenes.say_native: Uyga mehmonga borsangiz, kichik sovg‘a olib boring: gul yoki shokolad. Poyabzal masalasi uydan uyga farq qiladi: ba'zi uylarda yechiladi, ba'zilarida yo‘q. Shuning uchun so‘rang: “Shall I take my shoes off?” Ketishda “Thank you for having us” deb minnatdorchilik bildiring. Ertasi kuni qisqa rahmat xabari ham yaxshi taassurot qoldiradi.
scenes.say: When visiting a home, bring a small gift, such as flowers. Shoes vary, so ask: shall I take my shoes off? When you leave, say: thank you for having us.
scenes.say_uz: Mehmonga kichik sovg‘a olib boring. So‘rang: shall I take my shoes off? Ketishda thank you for having us deng.

scenes.title: Tinglang: uyga taklif
board: Emma: Come in! You must be Dilnoza.
Dilnoza: Thank you for inviting me. These are for you.
Dilnoza: Shall I take my shoes off?
Emma: Only if you like. Some people do, some don't.
scenes.say_native: Ikkinchi dialog. Dilnoza inglizlik hamkasbi Emmaning uyiga birinchi marta keldi. U nimadir olib kelgan va poyabzal haqida so‘rayapti. Emma nima deydi? Diqqat bilan eshiting. Emma qanday yumshoq gapirishiga qarang, u hech narsani talab qilmaydi va mehmonni erkin his ettiradi.
scenes.say: Come in! You must be Dilnoza. Thank you for inviting me. These are for you. How lovely! Shall I take my shoes off? Oh, only if you like. Some people do, some don't. Now, what can I get you to drink?
scenes.say_uz: Kiring! Siz Dilnozasiz. Taklif uchun rahmat. Bu sizga. Qanday go‘zal! Poyabzalimni yechaymi? Xohlasangiz. Ba'zilar yechadi, ba'zilar yo‘q. Nima ichasiz?

scenes.title: Dialog bo‘yicha savollar
board: 2) Does Emma insist on shoes off?
scenes.say_native: Uchta savol. Birinchi: Dilnoza nima olib keldi? Ikkinchi: Emma poyabzalni yechishni talab qiladimi? Uchinchi: oxirida Emma nimani taklif qiladi? Qisqa ayting. Javoblarni qisqa va aniq aytsangiz bo‘ladi, to‘liq gap shart emas. Eslatma: javob bergandan keyin ovoz chiqarib o‘zingizni tekshiring.
scenes.say: One: what does Dilnoza bring? Two: does Emma insist on shoes off? Three: what does Emma offer at the end?
scenes.say_uz: Bir: Dilnoza nima olib keldi? Ikki: Emma poyabzalni yechishni talab qiladimi? Uch: Emma nimani taklif qiladi?

scenes.title: Javoblar
scenes.say_native: Birinchi: gul, Emma “How lovely” deydi. Ikkinchi: yo‘q, “only if you like”. Uchinchi: ichimlik. So‘rash noqulay emas, hurmat belgisi. Emma ham “some people do, some don't” deb umumlashtirishni yumshatdi. Bu keyingi nuqtaga ko‘prik. Bu dialog bir narsani ko‘rsatadi: mezbon ham, mehmon ham bir-birini hurmat qiladi va noqulaylik paydo bo‘lmaydi.
scenes.say: One: flowers. Two: no, only if you like. Three: a drink. And notice how Emma said, some people do, some don't. That softens a generalisation.
scenes.say_uz: Gul; yo‘q, xohlasangiz; ichimlik. Emma some people do, some don't deb umumlashtirishni yumshatdi.

scenes.title: Yangi odatga munosabat
board: ✓ That's different from what I'm used to.

examples.t: That's different from what I'm used to.
examples.uz: Bu men o‘rgangan narsadan farq qiladi.

scenes.say_native: Madaniy xatoga yo‘l qo‘ysangiz, vahima qilmang. Odamlar chet elliklardan mukammallikni kutmaydi. Yomon odat: yangi odatni ko‘rib “That's weird!” deb yuborish. Buning o‘rniga “That's different from what I'm used to” deng. Xato qilsangiz, qisqa uzr va tushuntirish yetadi: “I'm sorry, I didn't realise. Where I'm from, it's different.”
scenes.say: Do not panic if you make a cultural mistake. Instead of, that's weird, say: that's different from what I'm used to. If you slip, apologise briefly: I'm sorry, I didn't realise.
scenes.say_uz: That's weird o‘rniga that's different from what I'm used to deng. Xato qilsangiz: I'm sorry, I didn't realise.

scenes.title: Hurmat bilan umumlashtirish
board: tend to · often · generally · many · some
in my experience · from what I've seen

examples.t: In my experience, many people tend to avoid conflict.
examples.uz: Tajribamga ko‘ra, ko‘plar ziddiyatdan qochishga moyil.

scenes.say_native: To‘rtinchi nuqta: madaniyatlarni hurmat bilan solishtirish. Eng muhim qoida: “all”, “always” va “never” dan qoching. Buning o‘rniga “tend to”, “often”, “generally”, “many”, “some” deng. “In my experience” va “from what I've seen” iboralari fikringizni haqiqat emas, shaxsiy kuzatuv sifatida beradi. Shunda hech kim xafa bo‘lmaydi va siz ishonchli eshitilasiz.
scenes.say: Avoid all, always and never. Use tend to, often, generally, many and some. In my experience and from what I've seen present your view as an observation, not a fact.
scenes.say_uz: All, always, never dan qoching; tend to, often, many, some ishlating. In my experience fikringizni kuzatuv qiladi.

scenes.title: Stereotipdan qoching
board: ✓ Many Americans tend to speak with more energy.
✓ I'm not used to British food yet.
scenes.say_native: Ikki xato. Birinchisi, “All Americans are loud” kabi qat'iy gap, bu stereotip. Uning o‘rniga “Many Americans tend to speak with more energy” deng. Ikkinchisi, didni haqiqat sifatida aytish: “British food is terrible”. “I'm not used to it yet” deyish muloyim. Fikringiz o‘zgarmaydi, faqat shakli hurmatli bo‘ladi.
scenes.say: Instead of, all Americans are loud, say: many Americans tend to speak with more energy. Instead of, British food is terrible, say: I'm not used to it yet.
scenes.say_uz: All Americans are loud o‘rniga many tend to deng. British food is terrible o‘rniga I'm not used to it yet deng.

scenes.title: Solishtirish bog‘lovchilari

examples.t: Whereas guests here stay for hours, visits in Britain are often shorter.
examples.uz: Bu yerda mehmonlar soatlab o‘tirsa, Britaniyada tashriflar ko‘pincha qisqaroq.

scenes.say_native: Qarama-qarshilik uchun “whereas”, “while”, “unlike” va “in contrast” kerak. O‘xshashlik uchun “similarly”, “both” va “like”. Muhim farq: “whereas” va “while” dan keyin to‘liq gap keladi, “unlike” dan keyin esa ot yoki olmosh: “Unlike my country, …”. “Similarly” gap boshida turadi va vergul bilan ajratiladi.
scenes.say: For contrast: whereas, while, unlike, in contrast. For similarity: similarly, both, like. After whereas, use a full clause. After unlike, use a noun: unlike my country.
scenes.say_uz: Qarama-qarshilik: whereas, while, unlike. O‘xshashlik: similarly, both. Whereas dan keyin to‘liq gap, unlike dan keyin ot keladi.

scenes.title: O‘zbekiston va Britaniya
board: Hospitality: big table vs small gift

examples.t: Unlike in Britain, hosts here often prepare a huge meal.
examples.uz: Britaniyadan farqli o‘laroq, bu yerda mezbonlar katta dasturxon tayyorlashadi.

examples.t: Similarly, family is very important in both countries.
examples.uz: Xuddi shunday, oila ikkala mamlakatda ham muhim.

scenes.say_native: Haqiqiy misollar. Faqat ayblamasdan solishtiramiz. Birinchi gap O‘zbekiston mehmondorchiligini maqtaydi va farqni ko‘rsatadi. Ikkinchisi o‘xshashlikni ta'kidlaydi. Ko‘rdingizmi, biz “better” yoki “worse” demadik, faqat “different”. Shu yo‘l eng xavfsiz va eng aqlli.
scenes.say: Unlike in Britain, hosts here often prepare a huge meal, whereas British guests may bring a small gift. Similarly, family is very important in both countries.
scenes.say_uz: Britaniyadan farqli o‘laroq, bu yerda mezbonlar katta dasturxon tayyorlaydi, britaniyalik mehmonlar esa kichik sovg‘a olib keladi. Oila ikkala mamlakatda ham muhim.

scenes.title: Bog‘lovchi tanlang
board: 1) ___ in Britain people queue, here it is less formal. (Whereas / Unlike)
scenes.say_native: Mos bog‘lovchini tanlang. Birinchi: “whereas” yoki “unlike” in Britain people queue, here it is less formal. Ikkinchi: “unlike” yoki “whereas” Uzbekistan, Britain is cooler. Uchinchi: “both” yoki “similarly” countries value family. Har bir gapda faqat bitta so‘z to‘g‘ri keladi, o‘ylab ko‘ring va ovoz chiqarib ayting.
scenes.say: Choose the best word. One: whereas or unlike in Britain people queue. Two: unlike or whereas Uzbekistan, Britain is cooler. Three: both or similarly countries value family.
scenes.say_uz: Mos so‘zni tanlang: whereas/unlike; unlike/whereas; both/similarly.

scenes.title: Javoblar

examples.t: Both countries value family.

scenes.say_native: Birinchi: “Whereas”, chunki keyin to‘liq gap keladi. Ikkinchi: “Unlike”, chunki keyin faqat ot bor. Uchinchi: “Both countries value family.” “Similarly” bu yerda ishlamaydi, chunki u gap boshida alohida turadi: “Similarly, both countries value family.”
scenes.say: One: whereas, because a full clause follows. Two: unlike, because only a noun follows. Three: both.
scenes.say_uz: Whereas, chunki to‘liq gap keladi; unlike, chunki ot keladi; both.

scenes.title: Farqni hikoya qilish

examples.t: I was surprised when the cashier asked how my day was.
examples.uz: Kassir kunim qanday ekanini so‘raganda hayron bo‘ldim.

examples.t: I later realised it was just politeness.
examples.uz: Keyin buning shunchaki odob ekanini tushundim.

scenes.say_native: Madaniy farqni hikoya shaklida aytish mumkin. Avval o‘tgan zamonda nima bo‘lganini, keyin nimani tushunganingizni ayting. Oxirida solishtirish qo‘shing: “In my culture…, whereas here…”. Shunday qilib hikoya ham, tahlil ham bo‘ladi. Aynan shu qolipdan uy vazifasida foydalanasiz.
scenes.say: Describe a difference as a short story. First what happened, then what you understood. Finish with a comparison: in my culture, whereas here.
scenes.say_uz: Farqni hikoya qiling: nima bo‘ldi, nimani tushundingiz, keyin solishtirish: in my culture, whereas here.

scenes.title: Uchta farq
board: Use: tend to · whereas · I was surprised…
scenes.say_native: Asosiy vazifa. Ingliz tilida uchta madaniy farqni ayting: salomlashish, mehmondorchilik, navbat yoki muloyimlik. Har birida bitta yumshatuvchi, masalan “tend to”, va bitta bog‘lovchi, masalan “whereas” yoki “unlike”, ishlating. Tayyor bo‘lsangiz, boshlang.
scenes.say: Now your task. Describe three cultural differences. Use a softener like tend to, and a contrast word like whereas or unlike. Start when you are ready.
scenes.say_uz: Endi vazifa: uchta madaniy farqni ayting. tend to kabi yumshatuvchi va whereas yoki unlike ishlating.

scenes.title: Namuna javob
board: 1) Britons tend to chat about the weather, whereas…
2) Unlike…, a vague invitation is not always real.
3) Guests often bring a small gift, whereas here…
scenes.say_native: Namuna. Birinchi: “British people tend to chat about the weather, whereas in Uzbekistan people often ask about family.” Ikkinchi: “Unlike here, a vague invitation in Britain is not always real.” Uchinchi: “In Britain guests often bring a small gift, whereas here we usually prepare a large meal.” Sizniki farq qilishi mumkin, muhimi yumshatuvchi, bog‘lovchi va hurmatli ohang bo‘lsin.
scenes.say: British people tend to chat about the weather, whereas in Uzbekistan people often ask about family. Unlike here, a vague invitation in Britain is not always real. Guests in Britain often bring a small gift, whereas here we usually prepare a large meal.
scenes.say_uz: Britaniyaliklar ob-havo haqida gaplashadi, bu yerda oila haqida so‘rashadi. Britaniyada noaniq taklif doim haqiqiy emas. Britaniyada mehmonlar kichik sovg‘a olib keladi, bu yerda katta dasturxon.

scenes.title: Qiziquvchan savollar
board: Would it be rude if I…?

examples.t: Is it usual to tip here?
Would it be rude if I left early?

scenes.say_native: Eng yaxshi himoya: so‘rash. Bu savollar sizni qutqaradi: “Is it usual to tip here?”, “What's the custom here?”, “Would it be rude if I left early?” Odamlar bunday savollarni hurmat belgisi deb qabul qiladi va mamnuniyat bilan tushuntiradi. Noto‘g‘ri tushunib qolgandan ko‘ra, so‘rab olgan yaxshi.
scenes.say: The best protection is to ask. Is it usual to tip here? What's the custom here? Would it be rude if I left early? People see such questions as respect.
scenes.say_uz: Eng yaxshi himoya — so‘rash. Odamlar bunday savollarni hurmat belgisi deb biladi.

scenes.title: Yakuniy takrorlash
board: Norms: small talk, queue, time, tips
Politeness: could / would / I wonder if
scenes.say_native: Jamlaymiz. Birinchi, normalar: small talk, navbat, vaqt, tip. Ikkinchi, muloyimlik: “Could you”, “Would you mind”, “I wonder if”, yumshoq e'tiroz va ohang. Uchinchi, xatolardan qochish: shaxsiy savollarni yumshating va so‘rang. To‘rtinchi, solishtirish: “tend to”, “whereas”, “unlike”. Eng muhimi, “different” deng, “better” yoki “worse” demang.
scenes.say: Norms: small talk, queues, time and tips. Politeness: could you, would you mind, I wonder if. Avoiding mistakes: soften and ask. Comparing: tend to, whereas, unlike. Say different, not better or worse.
scenes.say_uz: Normalar, muloyimlik, xatolardan qochish va solishtirish. Different deng, better yoki worse demang.

scenes.title: Uy vazifasi
board: Homework: Describe 3 cultural differences you noticed.
Use: tend to · whereas · I was surprised when…
scenes.say_native: Uy vazifasi: o‘zingiz sezgan uchta madaniy farqni ingliz tilida tasvirlang, yozma yoki ovoz yozib, taxminan oltmish so‘z. Har birida yumshatuvchi ibora va solishtirish bog‘lovchisi bo‘lsin. Muvaffaqiyat mezoni: biror madaniyatni yomonlamay, aniq va hurmatli tasvirlagan bo‘lsangiz. Keyingi darsda grafik va jadvalni tasvirlashni o‘rganamiz. Ko‘rishguncha!
scenes.say: Your homework: describe three cultural differences you noticed, around sixty words. Use a softener and a contrast word in each. Success means clear, respectful descriptions. See you next time!
scenes.say_uz: Uy vazifasi: sezgan uchta madaniy farqni tasvirlang, har birida yumshatuvchi va bog‘lovchi bo‘lsin. Ko‘rishguncha!

homework_uz: Sezgan uchta madaniy farqingizni ingliz tilida tasvirlang (taxminan 60 so‘z). Har birida yumshatuvchi ibora (tend to, in my experience) va solishtirish bog‘lovchisi (whereas, unlike) ishlating. Mezon: aniq, hurmatli, yomonlamasdan.

quiz.q: Which request is the most polite?
options: Would you mind lending me your pen?
You must lend me your pen.
quiz.why_uz: Would you mind + -ing eng muloyim shakl; boshqalari buyruq yoki grammatik xato.

options: A polite phrase, not always a real plan
quiz.why_uz: Bu ibora ko‘pincha odob; haqiqiy taklif kun va vaqt bilan aytiladi.

options: Would you mind to open the window?
Would you mind opening the window?
Would you mind open the window?
Would you mind opened the window?
quiz.why_uz: Would you mind dan keyin fe'l -ing shaklida keladi.

options: British people are bad at talking.
Many British people tend to be reserved.
quiz.why_uz: Many va tend to umumlashtirishni yumshatadi; all va never stereotip.

quiz.q: 'I'm afraid that won't be possible' means:
quiz.why_uz: I'm afraid bu yerda qo‘rquv emas, muloyim rad etish.

quiz.q: Choose the best word: '___ Uzbekistan, Britain has a cooler climate.'
quiz.why_uz: Unlike dan keyin ot keladi; whereas va while dan keyin to‘liq gap kerak.

quiz.q: In a US restaurant, a normal tip is about:
Your host offers more food and you want it. The best answer is:
quiz.why_uz: Inglizcha muhitda birinchi javob oxirgi deb olinadi; xohlasangiz yes, please deng.

quiz.q: Which is the best way to disagree?
options: I see what you mean, but I'd say it depends.
quiz.why_uz: I see what you mean, but... avval tan oladi, keyin fikrni muloyim aytadi.

quiz.q: When you see an unfamiliar custom, the best reaction is:
options: That's different from what I'm used to.
quiz.why_uz: Different neytral va hurmatli; weird salbiy baho beradi.
